subject: URGENT: GranitePay production latency & error spike after qprofile rollout
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@granitepay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@granitepay.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

Hi Kimberly -

We started seeing a sharp increase in P95/P99 latency and a growing number of 'model inference timeout' errors in production around 08:40 PT after you pushed the qprofile v2 -> v3 change. Summary:
- P95 rose from ~180ms to ~860ms; P99 from ~320ms to ~1.9s
- 0.8% of requests now return 503 inference-timeout, whereas baseline was ~0.02%
- Throughput dropped by ~18% despite steady traffic (we're not throttling)

This is affecting our checkout fraud scoring flow. We rolled back a canary, but the global switch happened shortly after and we hit the spike. We need an urgent rollback or mitigation; our ops team is holding all new customer sign-ups until this stabilizes.

Attached is a small sample of error traces and perf snapshot. Can you escalate? We're prepping an incident call.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Product Ops, GranitePay
emily.chen@granitepay.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: error_samples-20260818.ndjson (ndjson) — perf snapshot granule (zip)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@granitepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

Emily —

Thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm escalating this immediately. Rishi, can you confirm whether the qprofile v3 rollout included the new kernel selection path? If so, let's shelve that change and roll the customers back to qprofile v2 globally while we triage.

Lauren/Marissa — please join the incident bridge; we need a short executive note for GranitePay leadership and a rollback approval path. Neha, please capture the customer impact and SLA risk (credits exposure).

Emily — we will not move forward with any additional pushes until postmortem actions are clear. I'll set a bridge and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@granitepay.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

On the bridge now. Quick technical readout:
- The qprofile v3 introduced a more aggressive KV cache eviction threshold combined with a new fused attention kernel (opt-kern-3). Under GranitePay's request-length distribution the cache hit-rate dropped ~12%, which increases per-request compute and forces more serial attention passes.
- We also saw an uptick in transient OOM retries on some endpoints that trigger inference-timeout which bubble up as 503s. Logs attached (qprofile-diff.txt + perf snapshots).

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Roll qprofile -> v2 (config toggle) globally for GranitePay (fastest, ~4-6 minutes to propagate to their prod pool).
2) Pin runtime to opt-kern-2 for GranitePay (medium, avoids qprofile change but may not recover cache hit-rate).
3) Increase burst capacity (short-term) and accept higher cost while we debug (requires approval).

I recommend option 1 for speed. I'll prepare the rollback plan and sanity checks.

-Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@granitepay.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

Looping in Marissa for visibility to the executive team. Short executive note for GranitePay leadership:
- Impact: Checkout scoring latency and transient errors causing 15-20% drop in authorization throughput; immediate financial risk for live payments.
- Ask: Approve an emergency rollback to qprofile v2 (no code change, config toggle) while Redwood validates v3 behavior against GranitePay traffic patterns.
- ETA for rollback: 10–20 minutes after approval; verification window 30 minutes.

Marissa — can you approve the credit exposure threshold (Neha, please include worst-case estimate)? I'd like to send this note to their CTO/COO moments after rollback confirmation.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

Approve the emergency rollback to qprofile v2 for GranitePay. Prioritize speed and verification; we'll handle credits/comp later if required.

Kimberly — proceed with the rollback and confirm when the customer sees normal P99 metrics. Rishi — coordinate the rollback steps and provide a short post-rollback checklist we can run with their ops team. Neha — capture SLA exposure and start a draft statement for GranitePay leadership.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@granitepay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency + request errors after qprofile rollout (production)

Emily —

Update from yesterday's incident: we rolled GranitePay back to qprofile v2 at 11:12 PT (per Rishi's plan). Verification report:
- P95 returned to ~170–200ms within ~8 minutes; P99 stabilized at ~330ms.
- Error rate returned to baseline (~0.03%) after retries and cache warm-up.
- Throughput recovered to within 2% of baseline.

Attachments: granitepay-perf-snapshot-20260818.zip (contains before/after traces)

Next steps we committed to:
- Rishi's team will run an isolated profiling pass of v3 with GranitePay-like workload and produce a mitigations list (expected 3 business days).
- We'll schedule a joint test window before any subsequent qprofile rollout to GranitePay.
- Neha will follow up with a credit exposure estimate (if any).

Emily — thanks for the quick coordination. We'll prepare a concise executive summary for your CTO/COO and a technical RCA when available.

—Kimberly
